1 مَرِطَ , aor.
مَرَطَ , (K,) inf. n. مَرَطٌ, (S, Mgh,) He (a man, S) had little, scanty, or thin, hair upon the sides of his face, or of his cheeks; (S;) or upon his body, and eyebrow, and eye, in consequence of a weakness of this last, and of frequent shedding of tears: (K, TA:) or most of his hair fell off. (Mgh.) [See also مرت and مرد]. ＝
-A2- مَرَطَ, aor.
مَرُطَ , (S,) inf. n. مَرْطٌ, (K,) He plucked out hair (S, K,) as also ↓ مرّط , (K,) inf. n. تَمْرِيطٌ, (TA,) and feathers, and wool, from the body. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
